name: fantasy-hub
status_detail: Multi-league fantasy football tools. Every tool lives under /l/[leagueId] with leagues auto-discovered from Sleeper and format detected from settings.type (including type 3, which is Sleeper's undocumented guillotine code). Four live leagues: Dah Dynasty League (dynasty, in season), 2026 Half PPR (redraft, drafts Sep 7), Sunday Scaries #2 (redraft, full PPR, in season), and Dah Chopped League (guillotine, 16 teams, $1000 FAAB, still pre-draft). Guillotine leagues get a weekly FAAB advisor at /l/[id]/faab, /api/faab and a Tuesday email. Written playbooks with sources at /strategy. SURVIVOR is a live recommendation engine at /survivor and /api/survivor: no-vig moneylines from ESPN, real public pick percentages from Yahoo, first-place equity scoring and a season-long Hungarian assignment for future value.
next_steps: Watch the lineup tab through a live Sunday. Lock state is ESPN kickoff plus a corroborated Sleeper stat count, and neither has been seen against a full slate. Two things to check at 1pm: slots go to played at kickoff rather than when stats land, and no team locks before its game (a single stray stat row already caused that once, which is what teamsWithStats' threshold exists to stop).

His weekly post is the only source for a matchup that the schedule does not also carry, and week 1 proved it can be wrong (SF in four sections). The app now overrides it silently. If that ever needs to be visible, the place to count disagreements is fixtureMap's caller in lineup/build.ts.

Check the scorecard after week 1 settles (Tuesday, once Sleeper moves to week 2). It is the first real evidence on whether the lineup advice helps and whether the scoring adjustment earns its place. Shown at the bottom of the lineup tab; nothing appears until a week is graded.

Watch the first unattended Thursday email (2026-09-17, 8am ET, riding the /api/snapshot cron). This week's was forced by hand from a local run, so the scheduled path has never fired. /api/thursday-email?check=1 reports readiness with no auth and currently says willSend true, sendDay Thursday.
The full-PPR Lab 300 is coming: he says so in today's post. When it lands, Sunday Scaries #2 and Dah Chopped stop reading a half-PPR list and the skew warning disappears on its own

AFTER THE FIRST CHOP, verify chop detection end to end. It diffs this week's rosters against last week's snapshot in Upstash, so the first week stores the baseline and the second week is the first that can attribute players to a chopped roster. Never verified against a real chop.

SCORING SKEW IS STILL UNUSED OUTSIDE THE DRAFT API AND THE FAAB ADVISOR. lib/guillotine/scoring.ts scores raw Sleeper stat lines under a league's own settings and is reusable; rankings and player pages still assume one scoring shape.

notes: 2026-09-11: Caught a false lock in the morning's own fix, before Sunday. Sleeper's week 1 stat feed carried one row for Las Vegas, Bryce Cabeldue at offensive tackle with gp 1, for a game two days in the future, against 79/73/72/71 rows for the four teams that had actually played. The stats backstop read that single row as 'LV has played' and froze every Raider. It was not cosmetic: Dah Dynasty benches Tre Tucker and Jalen Nailor, so three flex slots were naming Jerry Jeudy (FLEX 125) as next best when Tucker (FLEX 108) was better and available. The backstop now requires corroboration (teamsWithStats, threshold 5, measured against that feed). The asymmetry is the reason it exists at all: a late lock costs advice Jack cannot act on, an early lock HIDES advice he could have acted on and shows a score for a game that has not happened.

2026-09-11: The matchup line said 'vs LAR' for Kittle and '@ LAR' for Stribling, both 49ers. Not a parser bug. An audit of all 257 ranked players found Jack's own week 1 post writes SF as 'vs LAR' in his QB, RB, TE and K sections and '@ LAR' in his WR section, with the Rams correct everywhere; four of five sections had the wrong half of one game, and no other team contradicted itself. The schedule decides this now, via fixtureMap next to lockedTeams (both moved to src/lib/nfl/week.ts, since the Atlas endpoint needs them too and neither is really lineup logic). His own row stays the fallback, so a player the schedule does not carry keeps what he wrote. Note this does NOT contradict the bye rule that his list beats team codes: that rule is about whether a player has a game, this is about which game and at whose ground, and a fixture list cannot be wrong about the second. Re-auditing caught a second one the fix had exposed: /api/jingles/weekly was emitting team 'JAC' from his post beside opponent 'JAX' from the schedule, so Cleveland and Jacksonville could not be joined up. Team codes are normalised on the way out now. All 32 teams, both sides of every game agreeing.

2026-09-11: Jack reported the lineup tab telling him to bench De'Zhaun Stribling out of a Chopped FLEX for Adonai Mitchell, when Stribling and Kittle had both already played Thursday night. Root cause was a missing concept rather than a wrong number: AdvicePlayer carried rank, injury and bye but nothing about kickoff, so adviseLineup treated every slot as editable forever and Sleeper's injury_status, which is never cleared after a game, still read Out on a man who had been on the field. Players now carry locked and actualPoints. A locked starter is seated before the superflex rule and before the solver and keeps his slot, a locked bench player leaves the pool entirely, and neither appears under Worth a look. Lock state is the union of two signals so that neither failing alone puts the bug back: ESPN kickoff and completed from the schedule survivor already caches (new src/lib/lineup/locks.ts, pure and tested), plus any team with a row in Sleeper's week stats (new src/lib/sleeper/stats.ts, shared with the scorecard, uncached because live scores move). Played rows show the score instead of arguing the rank. This also retires the impurity documented in scorecard/run.ts: the Sunday snapshot now grades a lineup Jack could actually have set, and only the raw counterfactual strips locks along with the adjustment.

2026-09-10: Two things on the lineup advice, both prompted by Jack questioning it. First, he asked why Kittle started over Brian Thomas when Thomas ranks higher, and the sentence deserved the confusion: it read "FLEX 108, 86 adjusted" against "FLEX 93, 98 adjusted", so the number that decided was second in both halves. Now the deciding rank leads. Second, and more important, measuring the adjustment before recommending a direction changed the recommendation: the points-per-rank gradient through the middle of his FLEX list is 0.043, while the mean scoring delta is 2.82 for a TE, so a tight end's delta was worth about 65 ranks. 139 of 150 players moved, and 61 of the 62 inversions of his order happened on margins under half a point. The adjustment now has to win by a point before it may reorder him, which is roughly the delta's own uncertainty. Implemented as an insertion pass over his order, not a sort, because a dead-zone comparator is not transitive. Effect: Pitts 66->60 rather than 66->49, and this week nothing in any league clears the margin. THEN built the scorecard, which is the real answer to accuracy: every Sunday morning it freezes what the app recommended before the lock, and after the week grades four lineups on real points (what Jack started, what the app advised, what Jingles' raw list would have set, and the perfect hindsight lineup). advised vs raw is what will actually settle the adjustment argument. A bug worth remembering: "is the week finished" was first implemented as "has any player scored", which was true on the Wednesday night of week 1 after one game and graded three leagues on mostly zeros. It asks Sleeper's NFL state now.

2026-09-09 (night): Waivers tab for the dynasty and redraft leagues, at /l/[leagueId]/waivers. Built because Jack asked who to claim in Sunday Scaries and the answer had to be computed in a throwaway script: the FAAB tool is guillotine-only. Separate tool rather than widening FAAB, since they answer different questions (surviving the week with money that never comes back, versus whether a player is worth a roster spot). Keeps the two halves apart on purpose: his WEEKLY list answers who would start on Sunday, usually nobody, and his SEASON list answers who is worth holding, usually somebody. It refuses to drop anyone this week's lineup depends on, refuses to name the same drop for several claims, and refuses to recommend a claim whose price it cannot state. Free roster spots are modelled. Reproduces the by-hand answer exactly: Denzel Boston #115 into the free spot, then Adonai Mitchell #118 for Tyrone Tracy #206. 14 tests on the pure ranking.

2026-09-09 (later): Two fixes on the same day the lineup work shipped. The bye check compared team codes raw, so Jingles' JAC never matched Sleeper's JAX and every Jacksonville player came back on bye, in week 1, when nobody is on bye. The first Thursday email told Jack to bench two starters over it, and excluding them also hid a real change (Sunday Scaries should start Trevor Lawrence QB 7 over Drake Maye QB 12). The team check now only applies to players he did not rank. Corrected email re-sent. Also built the lineup tab at /l/[leagueId]/lineup, second in the nav, changes above the fold and the full lineup below.

2026-09-09: Two weekly emails, one of which already existed. The guillotine FAAB guide has been running on /api/faab-email since before today and sent this week on Tuesday at 9:34am; Jack had not spotted it. The Thursday email is new: survivor pick plus only the lineup slots that need touching, sent for Week 1 today because the pick locked tonight. Getting there needed the whole weekly-rankings pipeline, which had never worked. Three independent reasons: the mailbox was not configured in Vercel (Jack fixed that today), detectScoring returned unknown because it reads raw HTML and an emailed post starts with Substack's stylesheet, and parseRankings returns ZERO rows on the weekly post because the row shapes differ from the Lab 300. New parser, new store (jingles:v1:weekly:*, never touching the season list), weekly posts exempt from the seen set because he edits them all week. Verified on the real post: 407 rows, no gaps, every row keyed to Sleeper. A scoring bug worth remembering: his post names all three scorings because it explains how to adjust, so the generic detector called a half-PPR list full PPR, which would have silenced the mismatch warning in three of four leagues. Two bugs only the real rosters exposed: slot permutations were being reported as changes (Dah Dynasty had five, all of them the same ten players reordered), and with two players coming out both slots named the first of them. notes.note: REFRESH CADENCE QUESTION TURNED UP TWO REAL BUGS. Jack asked whether injuries, news and pick percentages update weekly and said they should be daily. They were already better than that (lines, results and pick percentages on a 15 minute cache, injuries on 30, lazily refreshed on page load, cold load 0.6s and warm 0.05s, so no warming cron is needed), and that was verified rather than asserted: LAC moved from -600 to -625 across the session. But checking it exposed two failures that mattered more than the cadence. (1) SILENT PARTIAL FETCH. getSeasonGames caught a failed week and substituted an empty array, then cached all eighteen weeks for fifteen minutes including the hole. A missing FUTURE week quietly rewrites every burn cost; a missing CURRENT week makes currentWeek() skip ahead, so the page would have shown next week's board and invited a pick for the wrong slate. That is the worst failure this tool can have and nothing would have looked wrong. There is now cachedWithFallback in lib/redis/cached.ts: it keeps a seven-day last-known-good copy, validates completeness (all 18 weeks present, a Yahoo week covering 24+ teams, a non-empty injury list) rather than only catching throws, serves the last good copy on a short retry TTL when a fetch is short or fails, never overwrites a good copy with a bad one, and reports staleness so the page says so out loud instead of passing yesterday's numbers off as today's. Per-week fetches also retry once. The redis client is now built lazily behind a Proxy so the module is importable without env, which is what makes the fallback logic testable against an in-memory store. (2) YAHOO ONLY PUBLISHES THE CURRENT WEEK. The response carries a key for all 22 weeks, which is where the earlier and wrong claim of 'all 22 weeks of data' came from, but the future ones are empty arrays and past weeks drop off. That silently broke the calibration shipped an hour earlier: it fits the pool against the PUBLIC baseline for the weeks already played, and come Week 2 that baseline would have been gone, so alpha would have stayed at 1 forever with no error anywhere. Each week's public distribution is now archived to survivor:public-archive:2026 the first time it is seen, never expired, with live numbers merged over the top so the week in progress stays fresh and forgotten weeks are kept. Writes are skipped for drift under 0.05 percentage points. 28 new tests, 353 green.

SURVIVOR LEARNS FROM THE POOL NOW. Jack corrected two assumptions in the first build. He cannot see his pool's pick percentages until the week is OVER, which made the live paste box dead weight, and the pool also shows WHICH TEAMS THE FIELD HAS USED, which the research had flagged as the input that decides late-season weeks and which the first build ignored entirely. Both are now the same one-paste-a-week loop. THE PASTE IS RETROSPECTIVE: after a week ends he pastes what the pool picked, and that single input does three jobs. (1) It fits a CHALK FACTOR, one parameter, q_pool proportional to q_public^alpha, where above 1 means his pool crowds the favourite harder than the public does; it is fitted by golden-section search against Yahoo's distribution for those same past weeks and shrunk toward 1 by sample size, because one week is a coincidence and not a tendency (a single observation moves it only a third of the way). (2) It DERIVES THE BURNED MAP: the fraction of surviving entries carrying each team, which then scales that team's projected ownership, so a team 80% of the field has used reads as nearly unpickable by them. (3) It DERIVES ENTRIES ALIVE, because survivors equals entries times the share of the field on teams that won, so the number Jack was told to maintain by hand last session is now computed and the manual field is only a pre-season fallback. Invariant worth keeping: burned sums to exactly the number of weeks logged, since every survivor has used one team per completed week, and that is a test. Weeks whose results are not all in are refused rather than guessed, and a week where the entire field busted is treated as unscoreable rather than dividing by zero. The engine now takes Yahoo's WHOLE 22-week blob rather than one week's slice, because past weeks are the public baseline the calibration compares against; without them there is nothing to fit. Candidates carry a leverage flag when a big share of the field can no longer follow them onto a team. Also confirmed for the record: future schedule was already the core of the engine, the Hungarian solve runs on all 18 weeks of real moneylines, not ratings. 63 new tests, 325 green. Two test fixtures were wrong and the engine was right both times: a clock set before Week 1 kickoff, and a 21-7 scoreline written backwards so the team meant to bust was the winner.

SURVIVOR REBUILT FROM A CHASSIS INTO AN ENGINE. It had been pool config, checkboxes and six essays, with hardcoded 2026 power ratings and three phases of 'coming soon'. Jack asked for it to run itself and stay current on public pick percentages. Researched the format first (Bergman & Imbrogno's sequential-assignment paper, PoolGenius on expected value and pool size, the standard de-vig and spread-to-margin conversions) and then went looking for data, which is where the two findings that shaped everything came from. YAHOO PUBLISHES REAL PICK PERCENTAGES FREE: the Survival Football pick-distribution page ships all 32 teams for all 22 weeks as a JSON blob embedded in the HTML, unauthenticated, so ownership is real submitted picks rather than a model's forecast of them. ESPN'S SCOREBOARD CARRIES MONEYLINES: every 2026 week 1-18 is priced with DraftKings moneylines and spreads, no key and no quota, which retires the-odds-api item that had been sitting in next_steps since August. SLEEPER CANNOT BE READ: the pool is not in the public API (every pick'em endpoint 404s) and lives behind sleeper.com/graphql, which answers unauthorized without a session token; that was offered and declined in favour of one-tap logging, because a token that expires silently on a Saturday night is worse than five seconds a week. FOUR IDEAS DO THE WORK. (1) Equity, not safety: M = p(1-(1-r)^N)/r, where r is the fraction of RIVALS surviving given your pick wins. The common p/q shortcut is only correct if the whole field is split across your one game, and overstates leverage badly on a real slate. (2) De-vigged moneylines, always: -185 reads as 64.9% raw and 64.3% fair, and that gap compounds over 18 weeks. (3) Future value as a shadow price: the season is an assignment problem (one team per week, none twice, maximise total log survival) solved with a Hungarian implementation, and burn cost is how much the best path worsens without that team. (4) Both answers on screen: highest equity and safest board are shown side by side, because the engine will sometimes sell safety and Jack should see the price. VERIFIED AGAINST THE REAL WEEK 1 SLATE BEFORE ANY UI EXISTED, which caught two bugs no unit test would have. Future cost came back 0.000 for almost every team, and the cause was structural rather than a coding error: over an 8-week window you only need 8 of 32 teams, so removing any one never changes the optimum and the shadow price is always zero. It now solves the whole remaining season, which is a constraint that actually binds, with the published preference for a short horizon preserved by the discount weight instead (0.8 per week puts 2% on week seventeen). And the injury filter was WR and RB wide, so every single candidate carried three or four injury flags, which is the same as carrying none; it is quarterbacks and tackles now, two per card. A third bug was found by a bad test fixture and was real: a partial ownership snapshot had its missing mass spread over the few unlisted teams, inventing 31% ownership out of nothing, so coverage below half now degrades to an explicitly uniform field and says so. Also fixed: a.espncdn.com was never in next.config remotePatterns, so the old page's team logos would have thrown at runtime. 91 new tests, 275 green, no network in CI. One report object feeds the page and the API, same as the FAAB advisor. Strategy library rewritten to describe what the engine actually computes so the prose and the numbers cannot drift.

FAAB EMAIL IS LIVE LOCALLY AND THE DRAFT API NOW WARNS ABOUT SCORING. Jack answered the three open questions: draft is Friday Sep 4 at 6pm ET, which IS set on Sleeper (an earlier read of that field returned null and was reported as still unset, which was wrong: it was stale, not absent; the draft ORDER is what is still unset), send to jackhastings00@gmail.com, and the chopped roster definitely goes to WAIVERS, with only the drop time still unknown. Wired the Resend key and hastingsdigital.co sender that command-center and Website Builder already use rather than asking for credentials he had already given the machine; sending as faab@hastingsdigital.co. Two test emails delivered, which is the point of testing before the season instead of discovering a dead send path on a Tuesday. Because the drop time is the open question, the send day is now FAAB_EMAIL_DAY (day name or 0-6, America/New_York, default Tue) so answering it costs an env var rather than a deploy, and ?force=1 now sends even when there is no advice, so a manual trigger always proves the pipe. Two bugs the real send exposed: the skip message read 'Tueday and today is Wedday' from concatenating 'day' onto short day names, and a no-advice email had a blank league name and 'Week 0' because the fallback report carried no identity. SEPARATE FIX, PROMPTED BY THE FRIDAY DRAFT: /api/draft carried no scoring warning. The board is ordered by the Lab 300, which is half-PPR research, and Dah Chopped is FULL PPR with 4-point passing TDs, so Atlas (which reads the API and cannot see league settings) would have quoted half-PPR ranks at a full-PPR draft and sounded certain. It now returns scoringNotes from the guillotine scoring module, correct per league: Dah Chopped flags both PPR and pass TD, 2026 Half PPR flags only the pass TD, Sunday Scaries only the PPR. Verified the draft board itself works for the guillotine league: 274-player pool with kickers and defences already dropped, 14 rounds, 16 teams. FOLLOW-UP: Jack got the same email twice and was right that it was a real gap, not just my two tests. Nothing prevented a duplicate send: Vercel retries a cron run that fails or times out, and the send happens at the very end of the handler, so a retry after a slow Sleeper response would have delivered a second identical guide in production. There is now a send-once log in Upstash keyed on league, season and week (lib/guillotine/sent-log.ts), so a second call for the same week is a no-op that reports when the first one went out. ?resend=1 is the deliberate override, kept separate from ?force=1 because 'ignore the schedule' and 'send this week twice' are different intentions. Verified: first forced call sent, the next two were refused.

GUILLOTINE WEEKLY FAAB ADVISOR SHIPPED. Jack asked for a weekly guide telling him where to put FAAB in Dah Chopped, in the app and by email. Researched the format first (docs/guillotine-strategy.md carries the numbers and sources: Fantasy Life, RotoWire, DraftSharks, Footballguys, Fantasy Alarm, guillotineleagues.com, r/GuillotineLeagues), then read the league instead of trusting the published standard, which changed the design four times. It is 16 teams not the 18 every guide assumes, FULL PPR against a half-PPR Lab 300, 4-point pass TDs, no K or DST slots, and TRADES ARE DISABLED, so FAAB is literally the only way to acquire anyone. Also learned Sleeper now supports guillotine natively as settings.type 3, undocumented in their API reference and contradicted by their own help article; the app had been reaching the right answer by regex-matching the axe emoji in the league name. FOUR IDEAS DO THE WORK. (1) Elimination risk is a probability, not a rank: 20k Monte Carlo draws over every alive team's projected score, so the answer is 'you carry 12.5% against a 6.25% baseline' rather than 'you are 12th'. (2) A player is worth what he adds to your STARTING lineup, so the solver refuses to sell you a 9.4 tight end when your flex already starts a 9.4. (3) Pacing runs on eliminations remaining, not the calendar, because the published month-by-month curve was written for an 18-team league running to December and this one reaches the endgame around week 11. (4) Claims are grouped into chains that all drop the SAME player, making them mutually exclusive, because four independent claims that each look reasonable can all land and cost four times what you meant to spend. VERIFIED AGAINST REAL DATA by temporarily pointing the report at Sunday Scaries (Dah Chopped has not drafted), which caught four genuine bugs no unit test would have: the hold curve said hold 100% before the first chop, making week one unbiddable; the top-32 'championship' bar was computed league-wide, so quarterbacks (who outscore everyone) filled it and every spare QB read as worth 20% of budget, now a per-position bar; the candidate pool was a flat top-120 by projection, which in a one-QB league is nothing but backup QBs, now top-30 per position; and the posture text called 1.5x average risk 'about average' while Jack was the single likeliest team to be chopped. Also reframed the chop line visual after seeing it: a single line at the average low score put every team comfortably clear and read as safety, so the page now draws the BAND the line lands in (64 to 97 in the test week) plus each team's floor, which is what actually makes 12.5% risk legible next to a 112-point projection. 119 unit tests, vitest added to the project. One report object feeds the page, the API and the email so they cannot drift, which is the lesson from the draft board existing twice.

LIVE DRAFT BOARD IS NOW AN API (/api/draft?league=<id>), registered as Atlas source 2. The feature already existed on the draft page: live picks, what Jack has taken, which starting slots are open, pool ranked on the Lab 300. It just could not leave the screen, so during a draft the answer to "who do I take" was on a laptop he was not looking at, and he drafts on his phone. So this was extraction, not invention: lib/redraft/live-board.ts holds the assembly and both the page and the API call it, because two implementations of best available that drift is worse than not having the second one. Response leads with draft.started (a board for a draft that has not begun is a cheat sheet, not advice on the clock) and stillNeed in plain words. Dynasty is refused by name rather than answered. Verified live on all three leagues: redraft 287 pool, guillotine 273, dynasty refused. ALSO TODAY: Lab 300 v2.0, rank chip on every player via PlayerLink (gated by a new LeagueTypeProvider so dynasty shows nothing), and player=Name lookup on /api/jingles after Atlas could not answer "pollard or jacobs" because the API could only page from the top.

LAB 300 v2.0 (8/30) replaces v1.0 (8/16). Parsed from the PDF, not typed: 300 ranks complete, no duplicates, every player on a Sleeper id (295 kept, 5 looked up). 279 of 300 changed rank, 5 in, 5 out; Tee Higgins is off the list entirely. Final 50 tier is gone, so 14 tiers not 15. Two errors in his PDF corrected and only those two: Rhamondre Stevenson on "NET" read as NE, and the Bears defence listed on DET read as CHI. The second one mattered because Sleeper keys a defence by its team, so verbatim would have given the Bears DST Detroit's id. FORMAT SCOPE now explicit: Jack said twice that this is redraft and guillotine only, never dynasty. It had lived as a bare inequality inside one badge component and the API said nothing, which meant Atlas (which reads that API and cannot see the league) would naturally quote a redraft rank at a dynasty trade. Now one constant in the data module, read by the badge, and appliesTo plus a scope note on the API response.
